hero.tagline: Try the whole building-permit journey, from MitID login to the decision in Digital Post. Open source on Drupal 11. No licence fee and no charge per submitted form.

comparison.heading: What you get that proprietary alternatives don't offer
comparison.lead: Most platforms for digital case flows in the Danish municipal market are closed, licence-based and vendor-hosted. Here is how we differ:

row2.title: Visual modeler
row2.us: Open it, read it, change it yourself in the visual modeler

row3.title: Hosting
row3.us: Your own server or an EU VPS, ideally in Denmark. You own the data and decide where it lives.

row4.title: Pricing model
row4.us: The software is free. You only pay for hosting, operations and any consulting.
row4.them: Annual licence plus a fee per submitted form or case

row5.title: Dependencies
row5.us: Drupal 11 and well-known modules such as Webform, ECA and OpenID Connect

comparison.footnote: The proprietary alternatives do their job just fine. We do it in a way you can maintain yourself, without licence costs that grow with case volume.

workflows.title: Ready-made flows to build on
workflows.description: Building permit, parking permit, marriage booking, parental approval, complaints and more flows come included. Several of them can be tried in the demo, including a complaint about a decision.

multiTenant.title: MitID and NemLog-in via OIDC
multiTenant.description: OIDC with PKCE (S256), CPR pre-fill from the login and NSIS level substantial or high. The code is ready, but going live needs a certificate and an agreement with NemLog-in. The demo uses a mock IdP. NemLog-in Erhverv is on the roadmap.

danish.title: Digital Post (SF1601)
danish.description: The same code in four modes, switched with one setting: fake_db locally, WireMock in tests, and Serviceplatformen's test and production environments. Production needs a certificate and an agreement.

security.title: CPR protection
security.description: CPR numbers are encrypted at field level, and every MitID session and every Digital Post dispatch is written to the audit log.

workflowDemo.title: Case flows with several parties
workflowDemo.subtitle: See how ÅbenForms handles case flows with several parties and automatic integrations.

citizen.action: Applies for a building permit with MitID login. Name and CPR are fetched automatically, and the building address is validated against the Danish Address Register.

caseworker.action: Gets the case in their inbox, reviews the application and passes it on for technical assessment. Filing in an ESDH system such as SBSYS is prepared.

technical.action: Assesses the drawings against the building regulations and approves or asks for changes.

approval.action: On approval the permit is sent as a PDF via Digital Post.

eca.title: The flows run on ECA
eca.description: ÅbenForms builds its flows on ECA (Event-Condition-Action), an actively developed Drupal module, rather than the older Maestro.

benefits.visual: A visual modeler where the flow can be read and changed
benefits.flexible: Event-driven logic instead of business rules hard-coded in the code
benefits.headless: Headless: the frontend talks to Drupal over JSON:API

hub.heading: Try ÅbenForms
hub.lead: We do not ask for what we already know.
hub.body: Every demo is a real self-service flow: you log in with a mock MitID, we fetch what the municipality already holds in its registers, and you only type what only you know. Then the case runs and the decision lands in Digital Post. Every step shows which register we asked, on which legal basis, and whether the rail is live or demo.
hub.comingBody: This scenario is on its way. Building permit can be tried now.
hub.offline: The demo runs locally with a mock MitID. Book a walkthrough via Contact.
hub.honestBody: DEMO means test data, because the integration is not finished yet (e.g. CPR Family+ and STIL). LIVE-READY means the code is built and only needs a certificate and agreement (e.g. MitID and Digital Post). LIVE means AabenForms' own data, e.g. the case register. No demo fetches data from an external register today. The badges are the same as on the readiness board.

The address comes from the mock IdP's claims, which real MitID does not issue, hence DEMO.

commentary.login: The frontend sends you to /mitid/login. Drupal creates state, nonce and a PKCE challenge and sends you to the identity provider. Back on /auth/callback we exchange the code for a session.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/[form] (MitID session in the Authorization header, never the URL) runs the register lookups the flow would run and returns every value with source, contract, legal basis and audit number. The CPR always arrives masked from the server.
commentary.form: Only what the registers do not know is asked for. Choices from list sources (child, case) travel with the application.
commentary.workflow: POST to /api/webform/[form]/submit runs the ECA flow synchronously and returns every step. The identity gate checks the session on the server.
commentary.letter: GET /api/digital-post/recent looks up the Digital Post log for your session. In production this is an SF1601 call to NgDP.

klage.title: Appeal a decision
klage.story: Mikkel helps his mother Birthe. She logs in with her own MitID. The case, the decision and the appeal deadline are fetched, she only writes why she appeals.
klage.intro: Digital inclusion at the kitchen table: Mikkel sits beside her, but Birthe logs in with MitID herself. Her cases, the decision and the appeal deadline come from the case register, so she only writes why she appeals.

fetched.cases: Your cases with a decision (case register)

prefill.exempt: Birthe is exempt from Digital Post. Letters to her are therefore sent as physical letters.

option.chooseHint: Fetched from {register}. Choose the decision you want to appeal.

login.body: Birthe logs in with her own MitID. Mikkel helps at the kitchen table but never logs in as his mother. To appeal for her he can use a digital power of attorney (see the demo "Mikkel appeals on behalf of his mother").

form.body: The case, the decision and the appeal deadline are fetched. Birthe only writes why she appeals.

fields.begrundelseHint: Write what is wrong in the decision, and what you think the decision should be.

validation.begrundelse: Write why you appeal the decision

complete.heading: The appeal is registered
complete.body: The case now has the status Appealed. The receipt is sent to Birthe as a physical letter because she is exempt from Digital Post.

commentary.login: The MitID login gives the municipality Birthe's CPR number. It reaches the browser only masked and is filled in on the server at submission.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/klage looks up Birthe's cases in the AabenForms case register (live) with decision, decision date and appeal deadline. A case that is already appealed, or whose deadline has passed, is shown but cannot be chosen.
commentary.form: Only what the register does not know: why Birthe appeals. The case number carries over from the choice in step 2.
commentary.workflow: The ECA flow (klage_flow) validates the MitID session, checks the case belongs to the logged-in citizen, registers the appeal and sends a receipt. The case becomes Appealed.
commentary.letter: The receipt is sent as a physical letter because Birthe is exempt from Digital Post (the print channel is DEMO). Her digital inbox is therefore empty, as expected.

merudgifter.title: Extra expenses for a child with a disability
merudgifter.story: Freja applies for coverage of extra expenses for Emil. The children are fetched; she only writes about the need. Income is not fetched.
merudgifter.intro: Log in with the mock MitID, pick the child from the CPR register, describe the need and follow the decision to the letter in Digital Post. Income is not fetched: the section 41 benefit does not depend on the parents' income.

fields.funktionsnedsaettelseHint: For example the diagnosis and which extra expenses it causes day to day.
fields.maanedligMerudgiftHint: In the demo the threshold is 1,000 DKK/month: from 1,000 DKK the application is granted, below 1,000 DKK it ends in a refusal with appeal guidance.

validation.maanedligMerudgift: Enter the monthly extra expenses in DKK

medhold.heading: Granted: the extra expenses are covered
medhold.body: The amount is at least 1,000 DKK/month, so the flow granted the application, sent the decision letter and closed the case via SF2900.

afslag.heading: Refusal with appeal guidance
afslag.body: The amount is below 1,000 DKK/month. The flow ran the consultation of the party, refused the application, sent the letter with appeal guidance and started a 4-week appeal deadline.

neutral.heading: The decision has been sent
neutral.body: The decision letter is in Digital Post below.

commentary.login: The MitID login gives the municipality your CPR number. It only reaches the browser masked and is filled in on the server at submission.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/merudgifter fetches your children from CPR Family+ (SF6006, demo). Household income is not fetched, because section 41 does not depend on the parents' income (data minimisation). Every lookup is logged with its legal basis: Social Services Act section 41, Public Administration Act section 7, GDPR art. 6(1)(e).
commentary.form: Only what the registers do not know: the child's disability and the monthly extra expenses. The amount drives the decision in the demo: 1,000 DKK/month or more is granted, less gives consultation and a refusal.
commentary.workflow: The ECA flow opens and journals the case and branches on the amount: a grant is closed via SF2900, a refusal goes through consultation of the party and starts an appeal deadline. Income plays no part.
commentary.letter: The decision letter is sent to Digital Post (simulated). On a refusal it carries appeal guidance, and the appeal deadline has started on the case.

commentary.prefill: CPR Familie+ (SF6006) returns the children in Freja's custody and, for each child, who holds custody. For Emil it is joint with Lars Andersen, so custody and the other parent are not asked.

commentary.title: What's happening behind the scenes
commentary.auth: The frontend redirects to /mitid/login. Drupal generates state + nonce + PKCE challenge and forwards you to Keycloak.
commentary.form: We fetch /mitid/session/{id} and pre-fill the form with id_token claims. CPR is shown masked in the UI.
commentary.workflow: POST to /api/webform/building_permit/submit runs the entire ECA flow synchronously and returns workflow.steps in the same response.
commentary.inbox: GET /api/digital-post/recent looks up aabenforms_digital_post_log by SHA-256 of your session CPR. The letter body is sanitised server-side.

sygedagpenge.title: Sickness benefit
sygedagpenge.story: Mikkel has been injured and cannot work. His employer has reported him sick. The municipality fetches employment and pay, so he only writes what he cannot do and how long it is expected to last.
sygedagpenge.intro: Log in with the mock MitID, see the employer, working hours and first day of sickness the municipality already knows, write only what you cannot do, and follow the decision to the letter in Digital Post with the date of the first follow-up meeting.

fields.hoursMet: {hours} hours in the last {months} months - the {required}-hour requirement is met
fields.hoursNotMet: {hours} hours in the last {months} months - the {required}-hour requirement is not met
fields.sicknessDescription: What can you not do because of your illness?
fields.sicknessDescriptionHint: Describe what you cannot do in your job right now. You do not have to give a diagnosis.
fields.expectedDuration: How long do you expect to be ill?
fields.contactPhoneHint: The municipality may call you about the first follow-up meeting.

validation.sicknessDescription: Describe what you cannot do because of your illness

commentary.login: The MitID login gives the municipality your CPR number. It only reaches the browser masked and is filled in on the server at submission.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/sygedagpenge fetches the employer and working hours from eIndkomst (demo) and the first day of sickness from the employer's report in NemRefusion (demo). The municipality uses the pay to calculate the benefit, but it is not sent to the browser. Every lookup is logged with its legal basis: Sickness Benefit Act section 32, Public Administration Act section 7, GDPR art. 6(1)(e).
commentary.form: Only what the registers do not know: what you cannot do, how long it is expected to last and whether you are in treatment. You do not have to give a diagnosis. If you disagree with the employer's information, you tell the municipality.
commentary.workflow: The ECA flow confirms MitID, opens and journals the case and checks the employment requirement: at least 240 hours in the last 6 full calendar months and at least 40 hours in 5 of them. Met gives the right to sickness benefit; otherwise consultation of the party and a refusal with appeal guidance.
commentary.letter: The decision letter is sent to Digital Post (simulated) in plain language with the date of the first follow-up meeting. The date is 8 weeks after the first day of sickness - a demo simplification; borger.dk says the municipality assesses the case within 8 weeks.

complete.heading: You are entitled to sickness benefit
complete.body: The employment requirement is met. The employer pays for the first 30 calendar days, then the municipality pays. The letter below has the date of the first follow-up meeting.

klageFuldmagt.title: Mikkel appeals on behalf of his mother
klageFuldmagt.story: Mikkel has a digital power of attorney from his mother Birthe. He logs in with his own MitID and appeals for her. Her cases and the deadline are fetched, he only types why.
klageFuldmagt.intro: Digital inclusion with a power of attorney: Birthe cannot manage digitally herself, so she has given her son Mikkel a digital power of attorney. He logs in as himself, and the municipality can see whom he may act for. Birthe's cases and the appeal deadline are fetched, Mikkel only types why she appeals.

login.body: Mikkel logs in with his own MitID. His login tells the municipality that he holds a digital power of attorney from Birthe for appeals. He never logs in as his mother.

form.body: Birthe's case, the decision and the appeal deadline are fetched. Mikkel only types why she appeals.

fetched.fuldmagt: Whom you may act for (digital power of attorney via MitID)

fields.begrundelseHint: In Birthe's words, why she disagrees with the decision.

prefill.actingFor: You are acting on behalf of {name} ({cpr}) with a digital power of attorney. The cases below are hers, and the appeal is filed in her name.
prefill.noFuldmagt: Your login holds no power of attorney covering appeals. Log in as Mikkel Jensen to try the journey.

complete.heading: The appeal is registered in Birthe's name
complete.body: The case now has the status Appealed. The municipality has recorded that Mikkel filed it with a digital power of attorney. The receipt goes to Birthe, and Mikkel gets a copy.

receipt.actorValue: Mikkel Jensen with a digital power of attorney
receipt.letterPhysical: Sent as a physical letter (exempt from Digital Post)

commentary.login: Mikkel's MitID login carries a digital power of attorney from Birthe (in the demo a claim from the mock IdP, in production NemLog-in Digital Fuldmagt). It is kept in his session on the server and shown only with name and masked CPR.
commentary.prefill: GET /api/prefill/klage?subject=0 only points at the power of attorney the server itself holds from MitID. The server checks it covers appeals, looks up Birthe's cases and logs the lookup against Mikkel.
commentary.form: Only what the register does not know: why Birthe appeals. The browser never sends Birthe's CPR, only an index into the power of attorney.
commentary.workflow: On submit Birthe becomes the applicant and Mikkel is recorded as the person who acted, on the basis of a digital power of attorney. The ECA flow re-checks the power of attorney from the session before the case becomes Appealed, and sends the receipt.
commentary.letter: The receipt goes to Birthe. She is exempt from Digital Post, so it is sent as a physical letter (the print channel is DEMO). Mikkel gets a copy in his own Digital Post because the power of attorney allows it.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lead: ÅbenForms must be usable by everyone. This page shows how the citizen part of the solution meets the web accessibility requirements, and what is still missing.
accessibility.scope: The citizen part of ÅbenForms on aabenforms.dk: the front page, the contact page, the cookie page, the demo overview and the self-service journeys. The requirements come from the Danish web accessibility act, implementing EU directive 2016/2102. The standard is EN 301 549, which refers to WCAG 2.1 level AA.
accessibility.outOfScope: The caseworker and administration part is not covered. It has not been tested yet.
accessibility.status: The solution is built on the Danish common design system (DKFDS) and tested automatically. A full manual screen reader test has not been done yet, and some parts are missing. We therefore do not declare full compliance.
accessibility.testedIntro: Automated testing with axe-core (WCAG 2.0 and 2.1, level A and AA), last run without errors on 11 October 2026:
accessibility.tested1: the front page, the contact form and the cookie page
accessibility.tested2: the address field, also operated with the keyboard only
accessibility.tested3: a MitID-protected form in its login state
accessibility.tested4: the demo overview and each demo journey along the way and at the end
accessibility.gaps1: The front page still has a few elements outside the design system (an animated badge, a glass effect and a dark code card). They are being reworked.
accessibility.gaps2: The caseworker and administration part has not been tested.
accessibility.gaps3: No manual test with a screen reader and magnification has been done.
accessibility.gaps4: The tests do not yet run automatically on every change, but before every release.
accessibility.gaps5: You are logged out after 15 minutes of inactivity, and you cannot yet extend the time or save a draft.
accessibility.method: Self-assessment, based on automated testing and a review of the components against the design system. The statement was prepared on 11 October 2026 and is updated with every release that changes the citizen part.
accessibility.feedback: If you run into accessibility problems, write to {email} or use the contact page. Please describe what you tried, which page it was and which assistive technology you used. We reply within 10 working days.
accessibility.complaint: If you do not get a satisfactory answer, you can complain to the Danish Agency for Digital Government, which supervises the web accessibility act.
accessibility.complaintLink: Complain to the Agency for Digital Government (was.digst.dk)

banner.link: Read more about our use of cookies

page.title: Cookies on ÅbenForms
page.lead: See which cookies ÅbenForms sets in your browser, what they are for, and how to change your choice.
page.whatBody: A cookie is a small text file stored in your browser so the solution can remember something from one page view to the next, such as your language choice. A cookie cannot spread viruses or read other files on your computer.
page.listIntro: ÅbenForms currently sets only two cookies. Both are necessary for the solution to work, and neither is shared with anyone.
page.i18nPurpose: Remembers whether you chose Danish or English, so you get the same language next time.
page.consentPurpose: Remembers your answer to the cookie banner (accepted or rejected), so you are not asked again.
page.necessaryHeading: Necessary cookies do not require consent
page.necessaryBody: Necessary cookies are the ones the solution needs to remember your own choices. We may set them without asking first, and they are not used to follow you across websites.
page.mitidHeading: Your MitID login is not a cookie
page.mitidBody: When you log in with MitID, the server keeps track of your session. Your browser only stores a session id in its local storage (not in a cookie), and it is deleted when you log off or the session expires.
page.statsBody: We currently set no statistics cookies and load no third-party scripts. If we add statistics later, they are only enabled if you accepted cookies in the banner, and we update this page first.
page.choiceRejected: You have said no thanks to cookies.
page.choiceNone: You have not made a choice yet. The banner is shown at the bottom of the page.
page.resetDone: Your choice has been cleared. The banner is shown again at the bottom of the page so you can choose anew.
